classification.difficultyReason: Select and link corresponding, vertically opposite, supplementary and co-interior angles in six supplied parallel-line diagrams, including simple angle equations.

content.prompt: Find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ in these diagrams.

spec.description: Parallelogram ABCD with single parallel arrows on AD and BC and double parallel arrows on AB and DC. Decorative blue linework is replaced by house black.
spec.mathematics: Angle A is 30 degrees; angles B, C and D are alpha, beta and gamma.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles between parallel lines sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-30^\circ\\\alpha&=150^\circ\\\beta&=180^\circ-150^\circ\\\beta&=30^\circ\\\gamma&=180^\circ-30^\circ\\\gamma&=150^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle ABC with AC extended through C to D. Ordinary source blue edges become black.
spec.mathematics: Angle A is 40 degrees, angle B is alpha, and exterior angle BCD is 120 degrees.

answer.worked:
An exterior angle equals the sum of the opposite interior angles.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+40^\circ&=120^\circ\\\alpha&=120^\circ-40^\circ\\\alpha&=80^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Quadrilateral ABCD with BC parallel to AD and matching single arrows. Ordinary source blue edges become black.
spec.mathematics: Angles A and D are 50 and 45 degrees; angles B and C are alpha and beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only given angles and unknown labels appear.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles between $BC\parallel AD$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-50^\circ\\\alpha&=130^\circ\\\beta&=180^\circ-45^\circ\\\beta&=135^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle PQR with three matching single side ticks and PR extended to S. Both Q and R retain alpha labels. Ordinary linework is black.
spec.mathematics: All sides are equal, angle P is 60 degrees, angles Q and R are alpha, and exterior angle QRS is beta.
spec.answerVisibility: The repeated alpha labels and supplied 60 degrees remain visible.

answer.worked:
All three sides are equal, so $PQR$ is equilateral and $\alpha=60^\circ$. Angles on the straight line $PRS$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-60^\circ\\\beta&=120^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Right isosceles triangle ABC, A above C and B right of C; CB extends beyond B without an added printed endpoint name. Matching ticks, right-angle square and both unknowns are retained.
spec.mathematics: AC equals CB, angle C is right, angle B is 45 degrees, angle A is alpha and exterior angle at B is beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and unknown labels appear.

answer.worked:
The angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-90^\circ-45^\circ\\\alpha&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on the straight line through $C$ and $B$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-45^\circ\\\beta&=135^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle PQR on a slightly rising baseline extended through R to S; retain the printed 90-degree text rather than substituting a square.
spec.mathematics: Angle P is three-halves alpha, angle Q is 90 degrees, angle R is alpha and exterior angle QRS is beta.

answer.short:
$\alpha=36^\circ,\quad\beta=144^\circ$.

Use the triangle angle sum, then angles on a straight line.
answer.worked:
The angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac32\alpha+\alpha+90^\circ&=180^\circ\\\frac52\alpha&=90^\circ\\\alpha&=90^\circ\times\frac25\\\alpha&=36^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on the straight line $PRS$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-36^\circ\\\beta&=144^\circ\end{align*}$$
